prompt: A small clay jar of gold coins and jewels half uncovered in the dark soil of a plowed Galilean field, a wooden plow and the edge of a farmer's hand brushing the earth away, golden evening light, wheat at the field's edge (Matthew 13:44, treasure hidden in a field).

One single large flawless pearl resting in an opened shell on a merchant's dark cloth, glowing softly, a harbor of the Mediterranean (Tyre) with moored wooden boats blurred behind (Matthew 13:45-46, the pearl of great price).

A heavy fishing net full of many large silver fish dragged onto the pebbly shore of the Sea of Galilee at dawn, the net unbroken, a small charcoal fire smoking on the beach in the distance (John 21:11, 153 fish).
A single small lost lamb alone among rocks on a Galilean hillside at dusk, a shepherd's staff reaching in from the edge of the frame, the flock tiny and far away on the next hill (Luke 15:4-5).
A silver coin (a shekel / stater) gleaming in the open mouth of a freshly caught fish held in a fisherman's wet hands, a fishing line and the calm Sea of Galilee behind (Matthew 17:27).

Two tiny thin copper coins (lepta) in the open worn palm of an old widow's hand, about to drop into a bronze trumpet-shaped offering box in the stone court of the Jerusalem temple, warm light (Mark 12:42-44).
An elegant alabaster jar of precious nard perfume, its neck just broken open, fragrant oil glistening, on a low table in a lamplit house in Bethany (Mark 14:3-8).

A gold signet ring, a fine robe and new sandals laid out on a wooden bench in a family courtyard at evening, a welcome feast being prepared in the warm background (Luke 15:22, the prodigal son's return).
A single silver drachma coin glinting in the beam of a small oil lamp on a swept stone floor of a simple house, a broom made of palm fronds leaning nearby (Luke 15:8).
A single tiny mustard seed on a fingertip in the foreground, and behind it a large mustard tree in a Galilean field with small birds nesting in its branches (Matthew 13:31-32).
A small woven basket holding five round barley loaves and two small dried fish, on the green grass of a hillside by the Sea of Galilee, a crowd sitting far away in the soft distance (John 6:9).
A clay oil lamp burning brightly beside a small flask of oil, held ready in the dark by a doorway at night, a wedding procession's torches glowing far down the village street (Matthew 25:4).
